overlook_from_stage.view_arc: Open arc runs roughly from bearing 180 deg (Koyasu pagoda, S) round through 250 deg (Kyoto Tower, WSW) to about 330 deg (NNW). The city basin lies W to WSW; the Higashiyama ridge closes the view behind (E).

precinct.note: Roughly rectangular, long axis E-W. Ground rises west-to-east across the precinct from 44.3 m at the West Romon to ~50 m at the Honden.

structures.note: Vermilion two-storey gate at the east end of Shijo-dori; faces WEST down Shijo. Rebuilt 1497.

Gion-zukuri: worship hall and inner sanctum under ONE roof. National Treasure (2020). Faces SOUTH toward the Maiden.
The formal main entrance. Faces SOUTH onto Shimogawara-dori. Rebuilt 1879.

relative_offsets_m.axis_note: Honden - Maiden - South Romon - stone torii form a near-straight NORTH-SOUTH ceremonial axis (bearings within 5 deg of 180). The West Romon is OFF this axis, 92 m west and 39 m north of the Maiden, serving Shijo-dori. This is the key layout fact: the famous vermilion gate is a SIDE entrance, not the axial one.

kiyomizudera_layout.approach_axis: Niomon -> Saimon -> three-storey pagoda -> Todoroki-mon -> Hondo runs roughly WNW to ESE, climbing 104.5 m to 115.5 m over ~200 m.

stage_structure.verdict: CONFIRMED. The 13 m figure is right. GSI 1 m LiDAR gives 115.5 m deck minus 102.8 m bare ground = 12.7 m at the stage centre, rising to ~14.4 m at the outer corner where the slope has fallen to 101.1 m.
stage_structure.area_discrepancy_note: OSM polygon is 15.7 x 10.2 m = 160 m2. The usual 190 m2 figure implies ~15.7 x 12.1 m, i.e. it includes the strip of decking that runs under the Hondo eaves. Use 15.7 m wide x 12 m deep if you want to match the cited area.

uncertainty_register.detail: GSI 1 m LiDAR gives 39.0 m at Shijo x Hanamikoji and 39.0-39.2 m along Shirakawa/Shinbashi. Gion is ~39 m, about 8 m lower than assumed.

uncertainty_register.item: Kiyomizu-dera stage at 240-250 m ASL (brief's suspicion that this is too high)
uncertainty_register.detail: The stage deck is ~115.5 m ASL, not 240-250 m. The whole temple sits between 96 m (Otowa falls) and 122 m (Jishu Shrine). The 240-250 m figure is roughly the elevation of the Higashiyama ridge BEHIND the temple, not the temple itself.

uncertainty_register.item: Kyoto Tower distance from the stage, guessed at ~3.5 km WSW
uncertainty_register.detail: Actual 2.47 km at bearing 251.3 deg. WSW was right; the distance was ~40% too large.
uncertainty_register.confidence: HIGH on geometry; tower coordinate 34.987536/135.759339 is MED (not independently re-verified this session)

uncertainty_register.detail: OSM polygon = 15.7 x 10.2 m = 160 m2. Commonly cited = 190 m2. Chose to report both; 190 m2 implies ~12 m depth, which likely includes decking under the Hondo eaves. Picked OSM for the geometry and flagged the cited area.

uncertainty_register.item: Ninenzaka vs Sannenzaka boundary, and OSM way 710696944
uncertainty_register.detail: OSM tags way 710696944 (pagoda -> Sannenzaka head, 173 m, bearing 106.6 deg) as 三年坂, although it lies WEST of the Ninenzaka/Sannenzaka junction and functionally is the pagoda-to-Sannenzaka link. I kept OSM's split (Ninenzaka = the 143 m N-S lane; Sannenzaka = the 216 m lane south of the junction) and listed the connector separately. A different source may draw the boundary differently.

Only three OSM width tags exist in the whole route: Shirakawa-Minami 4.5 m, Ninenzaka 4 m, Sannenzaka 4 m. Every other carriageway width in the street table is my estimate, generally face-to-face minus 1.5-3 m for eaves, steps and frontage. Treat all unstarred carriageway widths as MED at best.

Measured by ray-casting to OSM building polygons, capped at 20 m. Where one side is a garden, park, canal or temple wall with no mapped building (Shirakawa-Minami 23.0 m, Nene-no-michi 10.4 m, Shimogawara 11.5 m), the figure overstates the enclosed width. Streets with continuous machiya on both sides (Hanamikoji 9.1 m, Yasaka-dori 6.3 m, Ninenzaka 6.1 m, Sannenzaka 7.4 m) are reliable.
uncertainty_register.confidence: HIGH for enclosed streets, LOW for open-sided ones

uncertainty_register.item: Step riser and tread on Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka
uncertainty_register.detail: Sannenzaka: 46 steps over a 32.0 m run and 6.0 m rise => 0.70 m tread, 0.13 m riser, 18.8% average grade on the flight. Ninenzaka: 17 steps over 15.9 m and ~2.5 m rise => 0.94 m tread, 0.15 m riser. Step COUNTS are from OSM tags (HIGH); the tread/riser split is arithmetic from way length and DEM endpoints and assumes uniform steps with no landings, which is unlikely to be exactly true.
uncertainty_register.confidence: HIGH on counts, MED on tread/riser

uncertainty_register.detail: Footprints are HIGH (OSM polygons) but no height is published in ja.wikipedia for the West Romon, South Romon, Maiden or Honden. No heights are asserted.

GSI returned 867.2 m for my Atago sample (true summit 924 m) and 209.5 m for my Daimonji sample (true summit 466 m). My coordinates are on the flanks. Bearings are indicative only; do not use these two rows for skyline placement without re-picking summit coordinates.
OSM node 4517278152, tagged natural=tree and named 枝垂桜. Assumed to be the famous Gion shidarezakura, but the tag does not say so explicitly and there is a second unnamed 枝垂桜 node 30 m away.
Left null in the landmark table. The Daidokoro-zaka approach was sampled instead (57.6 m at the foot, 68.7 m at the top of the 32 steps).

All elevations are GSI orthometric heights above Tokyo Peil (the Japanese national height datum), not WGS84 ellipsoidal heights. Consistent internally; offset by roughly +37 m from the ellipsoid in this area if you ever mix in GPS altitudes.

The GSI 1 m product is a bare-earth DEM, which is why it correctly returned 102.8 m under the Kiyomizu stage rather than the deck. In dense machiya blocks the ground return can still be sparse, so values inside built-up areas may be interpolated. Street-centreline samples are reliable; samples inside building footprints are MED.
